quest.title: The Shoemaker's Children Go Barefoot
quest.description: Breaking into the heavily guarded Fatui facility was unexpectedly easy...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.title: East of the Moon, West of the Sun

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Quick, {NICKNAME}, scooch over a bit and make some room for Paimon...
Wah! Wh—What are you doing!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—Huhh?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: For some reason, the container seems to already be occupied. It is also clear that the current occupant is most displeased to have uninvited guests...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ow-ow-ow! {NICKNAME}, are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Furious Fatuus
dialogues.text: ...What the— what hole did you all crawl out from!?

dialogues.speaker: Calm Fatuus
dialogues.text: Look, isn't that the thief we're looking for?
...Give it back! Y—You... That's my treasure! Give it back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What treasure? We didn't touch anything... We haven't even opened the last chest.

dialogues.speaker: Furious Fatuus
dialogues.text: Do you take us for fools? Putting on this "uneven spoils split" act in front of us...

dialogues.speaker: Calm Fatuus
dialogues.text: We'll take them all in — both her and her accomplices.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? W—Wait! We don't even know her!

choices.text: I'm here on a Harbinger's orders.

response.speaker: Calm Fatuus
response.text: Pick a more convincing lie, would you?

response.speaker: Furious Fatuus
response.text: That still makes you a trespasser. And we arrest those too!

choices.text: I was passing by and saw the chests...

talks.objective: Enter and explore the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After some effort, you convince the Fatui guard to go "take a break" elsewhere...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They're all empty! This is the only one left...

dialogues.speaker: Weary Voice
dialogues.text: We've looked up and down and haven't seen hide or hair of that thief. Where in the world could she be hiding...?

dialogues.speaker: Cold Voice
dialogues.text: Maybe she's gotten what she wanted and already made the big escape?

dialogues.speaker: Weary Voice
dialogues.text: Haha. That's not gonna look good on our monthly reports, let me tell you... or Poruchik Raskolnikov's...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Someone's approaching. Let's hide! Um, <color=#00E1FFFF>that container</color> looks like a good spot...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like a journal. Pretty careless of them to leave it out in the open like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Where do you think you're going?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you weasel! Trying to ditch us!
S—Say what you want! A true master thief only has her eyes on the treasure. I couldn't care less about anything else!

dialogues.speaker: Voice from Afar
dialogues.text: ...That way, hurry!

dialogues.speaker: Voice from Afar
dialogues.text: ...Got... Stay put...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew! Finally, we're safe... at least for now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, just our rotten luck! Paimon never would've guessed that the container... y'know, contained a thief the Fatui were chasing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We wouldn't be in such a mess if it weren't for her. Great, now the chest is gone, and we had to fight the Fatui...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh and, and! She even accused us of taking some treasure of hers. Lies! Lies and slander! Ugh, the more Paimon thinks about it—!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Speaking of...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Something I swiped in the dark just now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the treasure she mentioned? Uh, what should we do now?

choices.text: Let's take it to the lost and found.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... wait no! We don't even know if there is one around here, and, even if there were, it's not like we can just waltz in there, much less her!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Paimon wouldn't have cared as much if it were just an item from a chest no one owns...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We should find a way to return it... A—As long as it's returned to its rightful owner, everything will be fine!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But we've probably already caught the attention of the Fatui here, so a little extra caution could save us a lot of trouble!

choices.text: Let's just leave it here and pretend we didn't see anything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm, maybe she'll come back and look for it... but will she really?

talks.objective: Look for a way to exit the room

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, calm down! Things were chaotic back then and we didn't mean to take anything from you. And see? We're here to return it to its rightful owner.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—Anyway, we'll return it to you right now... Uh, how should we do that?

choices.text: Could you open the door?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She probably can't... Maybe we should just leave it here...
...You can't be serious. What is this cold indifference you're showing to a fair damsel in distress!? If it were Reed Miller, he would have rescued me in a heartbeat.

choices.text: ...Fair damsel?

response.text: A—Am I not one?
Hmm... You're also here for the Proof of the Cognoscenti, right? How about this — you help me get out of here, and I'll consider sharing some clues with you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think we'll do just fine without your clues.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. We can find our own way! We're very experienced in that department.
Huh? W—Wait, don't go! Then, how... how about information on Raskolnikov? Poruchik Raskolnikov. They say he's quite somebody here.
Though wreaking havoc here wouldn't be a bad play... It'd be just like how Reed Miller ransacked the governor's palace, took back the Sampo Mill, and stole the heart of the governor's daughter...
...Ahem! Anyway, I—I mean, it would be in your interest to claim your treasure with grace, no? The information I have will definitely help!
P—Please, I beg you, please help me! If Raskolnikov learns that I'm here... I...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you say, {NICKNAME}? Should we help her?

choices.text: We're already here, may as well.

response.text: Hah! Splendid! Today really is my lucky day! Now, I've already swiped an ID card off the guards earlier, so I just need the other one, and we'll be set!
I don't know where the other card is... but even if you find it, there's still the problem of <color=#00E1FFFF>getting it inside and placing it high up</color> to remove the barrier.

choices.text: I guess we can do it for the intel...
My name is not Reed Miller.

response.text: Of course you're not, hmph. No one in our time is his equal.

choices.text: Since you can see us, we'll just leave it here.

talks.objective: Look for the owner of the lost item

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Almost there... I need to make some final preparations. Hmm, "Goldfinch," if you're ready, let's go.
You two...! If it hadn't been you, I'd have snagged the Proof of the Cognoscenti and gotten away by now! And... you also stole my—

talks.objective: Find a way to rescue the girl

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice. Now we can return the stuff we took from you by mistake earlier.
I didn't expect it to go so smoothly... I even got something as powerful as the Moonstriders. I'm sure they'll come in handy later.
Speaking of, you aren't bad at all. Maybe just a bit shy of Reed Miller's level, even though we look the same age... And is that a chatty fae next to you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon's not fae! Paimon's Paimon, {NICKNAME}'s companion and guide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, why do you keep comparing us to some thief? We're properly registered adventurers!
Eh? Were you commissioned by the Adventurers' Guild to come here, then? Hmm, so you weren't... Makes sense, she did say she only told me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, this isn't exactly a commission from the Adventurers' Guild... Also, why are you getting so nosy? You haven't even told us your name, that's not fair at all.

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Name? Call me Netochka. Soon enough though, I'll be known as the reincarnation of the legendary thief Reed Miller, heir to the Great Treasure — Netochka, the Thief Extraordinaire! Hehe.

choices.text: I think "Honorary Knight" sounds better.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thief Extraordinaire is cool and all, but "Honorary Knight" just has that righteous ring to it. And... it makes Paimon happy to think about the old friends who use this title!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Anyway... You're not here for a commission, and you don't like Reed Miller, so why are you interested in the Proof of the Cognoscenti?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: ...Ahh, is this about the Great Treasure? No romance or destiny involved, just here for the loot?

choices.text: My destiny does not lie here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about you then? Aren't you here for the treasure?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Heh heh, well, I must say...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: "I kindly ask you to return the Sampo Mill, and all other ill-gotten gains stolen from the Frostmoon Scions, right this instant!"

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: "Remember, Nod-Krai is our Elysium, and we need neither gods nor pompous lords here!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, what are you doing?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Haven't you read "The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire"? *sigh* Never mind. Of course you haven't. I mean, who wouldn't fall for him after reading that?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I came across this book when I was still in Novokitezhgrad... From that moment on, I knew my mission.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Upon my arrival in Nasha Town, the very first person I met gave me a clue regarding the Proof of the Cognoscenti — that's destiny for sure!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Just as the oppressive, greedy governor here stole treasures from the Frostmoon Scions all those years ago, the Fatui now have seized things that don't belong to them.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I must retrieve the Proof of the Cognoscenti from them and find Reed Miller's Great Treasure, so that his name, now forgotten, will be held in esteem once more throughout the world!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh...

choices.text: Um...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Th—There's nothing wrong with that!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: And just like how Reed Miller had his trusty companions Shadow Weasel and Wagtail, your unexpected arrival must also be fate.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Otherwise, I'd probably still be stuck there, even if you hadn't taken my treasure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? So what exactly is this treasure you're talking about?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: It's a thief's starter kit that someone sold me at a "heartbreaking discount." However, none of the doors here have keyholes, so it's completely useless.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: That person was like a prophet from the old tales. She seemed to know everything about me and my intentions at first glance...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Not only did she prepare everything I needed, but she also pointed the way forward for me... just for me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Even Paimon wouldn't fall for that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean "Even Paimon wouldn't fall for that"!? But you're right. All that "heartbreaking discount" and exclusive information stuff sounds like a scam...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a minute, did you get all your intel from her? That's not reliable info at all!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: That can't be... She was so sincere, there's no way she was lying! Hmm... You just haven't met her yet, I think. When we get back to Nasha Town, I'll introduce you.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: As for Raskolnikov... Well, Poruchik Raskolnikov, I do know him. We knew each other back in Novokitezhgrad.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: ...But never mind him for now. We just need to find the Proof of the Cognoscenti...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: So let's get moving! Hehe, it's like we're Reed Miller the Thief Extraordinaire and his two sidekicks, Shadow Weasel and Wagtail, come again.

choices.text: I call dibs on Shadow Weasel.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that makes Paimon Wagtail? Wait... Why can't Paimon be Reed Miller?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Character assignments require careful consideration! Naturally, it's first come, first served. And since I was here first, I get to be Reed Miller.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Ugh, what kind of roleplay is this anyway!?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: ...*cough* You're right, it is quite juvenile. Then let's go with Netochka the Thief Extraordinaire and her Merry Companions, Goldfinch and Snowy Owl!

choices.text: Can't I just use my real name?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: But I think Goldfinch suits you perfectly! And Snowy Owl really suits Paimon too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Snowy Owl sounds... kinda cool? It's all mysterious and wise and stuff!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Hehe, so that's settled then?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Now we can focus on finding the Proof of the Cognoscenti. Earlier, I heard that the chest was sent to the <color=#00E1FFFF>dormitory</color>.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Those two Fatui didn't follow Raskolnikov's orders. They're definitely in for big trouble. He's always been a meticulous guy. Everything has to go exactly as he plans...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: You could call him a perfectionist. No matter what trouble comes up, he always manages to handle it methodically. Some people really admire that trait.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: ...Anyway, enough about that now. We've got that Proof to find... and I still remember the direction those two Fatui went. Follow me.

choices.text: Yay, codenames!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You think that's better, {NICKNAME}? Alright then. Hmm... Snowy Owl doesn't sound too bad. It's all mysterious and wise and stuff!

choices.text: You can be Shadow Weasel, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? No way! Wagtail clearly suits Paimon better. Wait... Why can't Paimon be Reed Miller?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Character assignments require careful consideration! Naturally, it's first come, first served. And since I was here first, I get to be Reed Miller.

choices.text: Then I'll be Reed Miller.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: No way! I was here first, so I should be the one playing Reed Miller.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon is the most unique character amongst us, so it makes perfect sense for her to play Reed Miller!

choices.text: So you're a die-hard Reed Miller fan.
I'm a practical person.
I'm the hero who saved the city from the evil dragon.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Well, I've heard stories like that, though they sound more like things children would enjoy?

choices.text: My title would leave you quaking in your boots.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Oh! I get it, you're just trying to act tough. It's fine to be a nobody, as long as you make something of yourself later, like me!

dialogues.speaker: Cold Voice
dialogues.text: Just lock her up here? Is that what we're doing?

dialogues.speaker: Weary Voice
dialogues.text: Yep. Poruchik Raskolnikov's orders.
...Did you say "Raskolnikov"?

dialogues.speaker: Weary Voice
dialogues.text: That's "Poruchik Raskolnikov" to you, thief. Show some respect.

dialogues.speaker: Cold Voice
dialogues.text: Forget about her. Where's the chest? Have you delivered it to the <color=#00E1FFFF>archives</color>?

dialogues.speaker: Weary Voice
dialogues.text: Oh, Bakunin's on leave today. I bet he's downing another cup at The Flagship right now.

dialogues.speaker: Cold Voice
dialogues.text: He sure knows how to enjoy life... Let's leave the chest in the <color=#00E1FFFF>dormitory</color> for now and worry about it tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Netochka... Are you sure it's this way? It looks dangerous...

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Trust me, this is definitely the right way. Besides, isn't sneaking across rooftops what cool rogues do? Ahem... We need to keep our voices down.

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Snowy Owl. I'm here with you. Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: (I'll leave the one on the right to you, Goldfinch!)

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: (Oh, I didn't expect the Moonstriders to come in handy so soon. I'll take care of the top, watch this!)

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Piece of cake! Are you all okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't expect you to be this good, Netochka...

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Of course! How else would I live up to the title of the great Reed Miller, returned to Teyvat at last?

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: You can count on me from now on, heh heh.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How did we end up on the other side? We followed the floor plan exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Raskolnikov
dialogues.text: Do ants in a maze know that they travel along pre-designed paths? I am surprised that you took the bait without a speck of doubt.

dialogues.speaker: Raskolnikov
dialogues.text: You've fallen right into my trap, little thief.

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Raskolnikov...

dialogues.speaker: Raskolnikov
dialogues.text: It's Poruchik Raskolnikov. It's been a while, Netochka. I never expected Police Chief Stalanov's daughter to end up playing thief in this godforsaken place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Police Chief's daughter?

dialogues.speaker: Raskolnikov
dialogues.text: It seems these two playmates in your game of house don't know you very well. Not that it matters.

dialogues.speaker: Raskolnikov
dialogues.text: I must say, your little farce helped me root out quite a few deceptive, two-faced subordinates.

dialogues.speaker: Raskolnikov
dialogues.text: Organization members who fail to execute orders to the letter should be terminated, immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Never mind Netochka's background. We've met lots of odd ducks — so what if she's the police chief's daughter?

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Snowy Owl...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And all that talk about executing orders to the letter... You're all just moving a chest back and forth! The one giving nonsensical orders is the real weirdo here.

choices.text: Such a terrible waste of manpower...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! All this nonsense almost made Paimon forget that — that's what's important here!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: And it doesn't belong to the Fatui. I must take it back — that's my mission!

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: Take it back? Ridiculous. Of course Reed Miller's treasure doesn't belong to the Fatui — it belongs to Her Majesty the Tsaritsa.

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: Whoever brings the Great Treasure back to Snezhnograd will be rewarded. Should I do so, I could even be promoted to staff officer.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I knew it. You're as obsessed with these titles as ever.

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: ...Enough! Since you claim to be Reed Miller's successor, you must be prepared to follow in his footsteps too.

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: This place shall be your execution ground. If you have any last words, now is the time.

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: But I will not relay them to Chief Stalanov on your behalf. It's best that he never finds out what happened to his precious daughter. I owe my former teacher this much respect.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Precious daughter? Feh. All he ever cares about are his endless cases and "promising juniors" like you!

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: ...Hah, you're no better. Still as arrogant as ever.

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: But it matters little, because this will all end shortly.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Ugh...

choices.text: So, you really don't know who I am?

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: So long as you're an accomplice of the thief illegally infiltrating the Experimental Design Bureau, this place will be your grave too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like we'll have to do this the hard way...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I'm sorry, I lied to you. I do know him, but none of what I know will help us. I can't even help much in battle...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #There's no point saying that now, Netochka. Just leave the fighting to us... to {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I knew it would end up like this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But you prefer things this way, right? Straight-up fights are better than wild chest hunts... Whoa, watch out!

choices.text: Mere Fatui joiners...
Hand over the Proof of the Cognoscenti.

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: It's just down here and inside. I'll split off now. Goldfinch, Snowy Owl, don't get lost now!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Netochka scales the walls and roof with the power of the Moonstriders and vanishes from sight...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Looks like she's having the time of her life... {NICKNAME}, let's hurry and catch up.

dialogues.speaker: "■■■■■■ Technology Research"
dialogues.text: (No usable information can be discerned...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Paimon can see something from here...

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Looks like the disposal workshop. It's on the floor plan too. I guess this is where they get rid of defective products.

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Look up, I think I see someone...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Zoom in on the scene.)

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: It's Raskolnikov! And the chest!

choices.text: "Sir, the Proof of the Cognoscenti has been recovered."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Good work, you've done well. Rest up before the next assignment. Ah, and let's have Nod-Krai Hot Dogs for dinner tonight."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Wait. Why did Paimon get so caught up in acting?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Looks like you're both masters of disguise and infiltration, Goldfinch, Snowy Owl. You sure are reliable partners.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: However, it would be better if you both were more committed to playing the characters, in terms of speech and mannerisms...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? What are you, a film director? That's asking way too much!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Huh? This is nothing compared to what's required of ballet performers!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you watch ballet? Paimon thought you only watched... Wait, that's not the point here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, let's put the roleplay aside for now. We can pretty much confirm that the guy called Ras... Ras-whatever, has retrieved the Proof of the Cognoscenti, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, why are the Fatui collecting the Proof? Are they also interested in the Great Treasure? ...C—Could they be in the middle of a financial crisis!?

choices.text: That's what happens when you spend money recklessly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... It's hard to imagine that the Fatui would take interest in the Great Treasure because they're out of funds...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this that Ras guy's personal interest, then? Wow, asking his subordinates to find treasure for him, that's...

choices.text: Despicable!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do they call this again... Yes, that's it!— an "abuse of power"! Truly despicable!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Um... If it's the Raskolnikov I know, he wouldn't do this out of personal interest. In fact, he doesn't have anything that could even be considered a "personal interest."

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: There must be some motive... The only thing he's interested in is getting ahead of the game, so maybe he plans to bribe his superior using the Great Treasure...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come to think of it, Paimon never asked... What exactly is your relationship with that guy, Netochka? It's unusual for a thief to know so much about a Fatui officer.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: ...W—We just knew each other from before. We're both from Novokitezhgrad, so it's not that strange that we know each other, right?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Besides, think about it — no one ever questioned why the fae governor in the story wanted to seize the Sampo Mill, right?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Point is, the mill didn't belong to him, just like how the Proof of the Cognoscenti doesn't belong to the Fatui. So naturally, we — the ones on the side of justice — must take it back.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Goldfinch, Snowy Owl, this is where we carve our names in fame and glory as Reed Miller's successors!

choices.text: For fame and glory!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, if {NICKNAME}... if Goldfinch says so!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But that guy is also an officer here, right? How are we supposed to get the Proof from him without exposing ourselves...?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Hmm... Based on the floor plan, we can quickly get to the second floor of the disposal workshop from the archives, and get it done before he leaves.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: He thinks everything is under his control, including the chest, which ended up in his hands just as he wanted. But he can't control us...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Hehe, that'll be so Reed Miller! Appearing at unexpected times and places, making a dashing entrance, then gracefully departing... A perfect performance.

choices.text: For the Great Treasure!
Living the dream!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, yeah! Reaping the fruits of other people's labor while lounging on a comfy chair...

choices.text: Doesn't sound very likely...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right... Building a huge structure here and deploying so many people doesn't sound like financial crisis to Paimon at all.

choices.text: "I brought the goods. What about you?"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "What's the rush? Are you telling me how to do my job?"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Hmm, this is indeed what we agreed upon. As for what we brought, if you want to inspect them... come right this way."

talks.objective: Look for clues inside the dormitory

dialogues.speaker: Raskolnikov
dialogues.text: What!? How...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Paimon knows! This is what they call "Turning their own blade unto them"!

dialogues.speaker: Raskolnikov
dialogues.text: ...It seems I've miscalculated. The Proof of the Cognoscenti that you seek is in my hands. If you want it, follow me outside!

dialogues.speaker: Raskolnikov
dialogues.text: I'll be waiting for you at the highest point of the Experimental Design Bureau.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh!? He ran away? That... that coward!

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Leave it to me! I'll go after him!

dialogues.speaker: Bed
dialogues.text: (There's clearly no chest on the bed, so maybe under it... Whoa, no chest in sight, and completely spotless, to boot...)

dialogues.speaker: Container
dialogues.text: (A container that is just here for some reason.)

dialogues.speaker: Container
dialogues.text: (Reminds me of the time Netochka, red as a beet, pushing us out during our previous attempt at hiding inside one...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems the Proof of the Cognoscenti isn't here. At least, the chest containing it isn't.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But look, at least we found a floor plan of this place. Paimon's not sure how useful it'll be, though...

choices.text: How terribly careless of them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right? How could they just leave something like this out in the open?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: ...But if it's not here, where else could it be? Should I check the archives again? Or...

response.speaker: Voice from Afar
response.text: Haha! Seriously? I've been itching to see him eat crow!

response.speaker: Another Voice from Afar
response.text: Of course it's real. You know what Poruchik Raskolnikov is like. You think he's going to let someone get away with a fumble like that?

response.speaker: Voice from Afar
response.text: Tell me about it. I had a minor slip-up at work before... It wasn't a big deal, but I got slammed over it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Are they getting closer or something?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: We can't let them see us. Let's improvise and hide. Gotta look for a good spot...

choices.text: I'll hide under the bed.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The voices and footsteps get closer and closer. No time to hesitate — You pick your spots and hold your breath...

response.speaker: Another Voice Nearby
response.text: Huh? Where's the floor plan? I thought I left it right here.

response.speaker: Voice Nearby
response.text: You don't see it? Did you lose it somewhere in the <color=#00E1FFFF>archives</color> when we were moving the chest earlier?

response.speaker: Another Voice Nearby
response.text: I don't think so? Maybe I lost it back at the mess hall... *sigh* Man, fine, I'll go back and look. Wouldn't want to get into trouble again.

response.speaker: Voice Nearby
response.text: Thought you said the thief and her lackeys were gone? Heh, for all you know, we'll soon have Dhabit's little crooks peddling copies of the floor plan up and down Nasha Town!

response.speaker: Another Voice Nearby
response.text: ...Don't scare me like that. That's it, let's split up and look for it.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The voices and footsteps fade away. You carefully exit your hiding spots...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Ugh... Had to hold my sneeze in with all that dust...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's pretty clean and spacious under the bed, but we were completely exposed. That got Paimon's heart racing for a moment...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You should have hidden with us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh. We would've made it, just about.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: #Huh!? {M#That... Th—That's a bit too close, Goldfinch! A—Are you an idiot!?}{F#E—Even if we're both girls, Goldfinch, that's still too close...}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Netochka... {M#Only idiots call other people an idiot out of nowhere! Wait, what does that have to do with anything...?}{F#It's just for a second, what's the big deal?}

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I—In any case, keeping a polite distance is only p—proper! I—It's about etiquette, I'll have you know!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Aren't we intimate companions?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Intimate!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't think we're intimate yet! But we can be considered companions. C—Can't we?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We're roleplaying companions, if nothing else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That we are. Ahem. Well! Goldfinch and Snowy Owl are ready here! What about you, great Netochka? Are you ready to keep looking for the Proof of the Cognoscenti?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: ...Phew, g—give me a moment. Um, they ended up moving the chest to the <color=#00E1FFFF>archives</color>. We should be able to find it there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* We've been all over the shop looking for this thing... Paimon would rather take a commission from the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: This is the key to the secret of the Great Treasure! You can't simply compare it to commissions from the Guild!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Besides, we have the floor plan now... That's our "treasure map," no? Come, Goldfinch, Snowy Owl, let's be on our way!

choices.text: I'll take the container this time.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The voices and footsteps get closer and closer. No time to hesitate — You pick your spots and hold your breath...

response.speaker: Another Voice Nearby
response.text: Huh? Where's the floor plan? I thought I left it right here.

response.speaker: Voice Nearby
response.text: You don't see it? Did you lose it somewhere in the <color=#00E1FFFF>archives</color> when we were moving the chest earlier?

response.speaker: Another Voice Nearby
response.text: I don't think so? Maybe I lost it back at the mess hall... *sigh* Man, fine, I'll go back and look. Wouldn't want to get into trouble again.

response.speaker: Another Voice Nearby
response.text: ...Don't scare me like that. That's it, let's split up and look for it.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The voices and footsteps fade away. You carefully exit your hiding spots...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *cough* *cough*... F—Finally out... Who would've thought it'd be so dusty inside!? What on earth was it used for anyway?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Looks like my lucky streak continues. It's dust-free under the bed.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Should've squeezed in with you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It would have been a bit tight, but we would've managed...?

choices.text: Someone in Nasha Town would probably buy it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Guess it'll go to the highest bidder, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: F—Finally made it up here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's alone? Paimon thought he ran so fast because he was going to call for reinforcements.

choices.text: An ambush, perhaps...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! How despicable!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I'll... I'll fight with you!

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: If you want the Proof of the Cognoscenti, you must defeat me first! That is, if you can.

choices.text: Then he will have to pay the price for his arrogance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looking down on us... We'll show him!

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Phew... We won. Now, hand the Proof over.

dialogues.speaker: Raskolnikov
dialogues.text: ...Come and get it yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't expect you to admit defeat so easily... And there really weren't any reinforcements!

choices.text: This is good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sure saves a lot of trouble, but this isn't what usually happens. If this is a trap...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Didn't you say you'd get promoted if you brought the Great Treasure back to Snezhnograd? Why are you giving us the Proof so easily?

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: When did I ever say that I would be the one to do that? Keeping the Proof at the Design Bureau will bring nothing but trouble.

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: As long as it stays here, there will be an endless swarm of rats coveting it, trying to infiltrate this supposedly impregnable stronghold, just like you lot.

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: I am to guard the Design Bureau and ensure its efficient operation. But orders from my superiors must be obeyed.

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: This already constitutes insubordination, of course... but due to my failings, the Proof of the Cognoscenti that we spent so much manpower to find was ultimately stolen by a petty thief.

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: Now you can go back to Nasha Town... or wherever you want, to announce your victory.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: ...Did you lose to us on purpose?

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: Losing to an opponent who has deep ties with the Harbingers brings no shame upon me. I'm impressed you managed to find such help...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So you did know about us.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Eh!? I knew that you were exceptionally skilled, Goldfinch, but...

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: ...Haha! A fool blessed with blind luck. I've always hated your kind...

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: Forget it. Take the Proof of the Cognoscenti. The Experimental Design Bureau will no longer devote manpower to searching for this accursed thing. We won't meet again.

response.speaker: Raskolnikov
response.text: But if you insist on future unwelcome visitation, I'll show you what I'm really made of.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Raskolnikov leaves...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: This curtain call is completely different from what I imagined, even with the Proof of the Cognoscenti...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I need some time to think about all this...

choices.text: Things going so smoothly makes me uneasy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C—Could this be the trigger for an even bigger trap!?

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: If only he were the big bad governor oppressing the innocent, then I would have... Now, I'm made to look like the unreasonable child...

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm sorry for dragging you into this farce. Say, do you really have connections to the Harbingers? That's... a surprise. If you'd told me earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: #We could have been called "{NICKNAME} the Thief Extraordinaire and {M#His}{F#Her} Merry Companions" or "Paimon the Thief Extraordinaire and Her Merry Companions"... or something similar? Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Right, speaking of which, you should take the Proof of the Cognoscenti. Yes, it's much better in your hands than mine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do you sound so defeated all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, why are you giving up already? And, didn't something like this happen just a moment ago?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You and that Ras-whatever guy, you talk in circles around each other and act like everything's settled afterwards.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And that makes Paimon feel kinda uneasy, even if we did get the Proof! It's like a sneeze that just won't come out...

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: I just... suddenly realized that, compared to Raskolnikov and all of you, I'm just an insignificant character in the story, like I've always been...

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: I wish I could become Reed Miller, a true protagonist with an adventure to call my own — someone who can claim the spotlight and receive the adoration of all...

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: So I told myself that it was my destiny to become Reed Miller's successor. To turn my fantasy into reality, I came here in search of clues about the Great Treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Back in Nasha Town, Hidimbi gave me some clues on the Proof of the Cognoscenti and said I was special, that she had chosen me. I was so happy at the time...

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: But now that I think about it, how could I possibly have been the only one? She must have had other motives.

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: All that talk about being Reed Miller's successor, about destiny and mission... they were never meant for me. I'm still just a pebble by the roadside, worthless and unnoticed...

choices.text: You write your own story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, how does that saying go... "Everyone's the protagonist of their own story"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what's wrong with us being "Netochka the Thief Extraordinaire and Her Merry Companions" in your story?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, but like we agreed, Snowy Owl is the character who embodies wisdom and beauty, and who's just the slightest bit mysterious! It's a role made for Paimon, hehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #As for {NICKNAME}... Sorry, Goldfinch, {M#he}{F#she} can be the {M#handsome}{F#beautiful} and cool character!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I envy you, Paimon... I wish I could think that way. Do you have any tips on finding happiness?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm... Well, Paimon's happy just being with {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Whether it's eating Chicken-Mushroom Skewers in the wild or feasting in a fancy restaurant, it's all good as long as it's done with {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: #So if I want to be happy like you, Paimon, I'd need a companion like {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... That doesn't sound right. Why do you always have to imitate others, Netochka?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You just have to be yourself. Everyone has a chance of becoming Reed Miller's successor, but only you can be you.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: But if I'm just being myself... would I actually deserve it? To be a brilliant character in people's eyes, or a special someone?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, why are you still going on about this? It doesn't matter what others think!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't get why you keep worrying over it. Even if you're not someone's "special someone" or a big name, you can still be happy!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: So you think none of that matters... That's really broad-minded, Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Broad-minded? Hmm, yeah, that's right! That's the secret to happiness! Hehe, Paimon can drop insightful lines too.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: #Well, since you think none of that matters, then... {NICKNAME}, would you become my best companion? I don't expect to be your special someone, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Wait a minute! B—Best companion? That won't do!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That title belongs to Paimon, r—right? {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Haha, you talk the talk but can't walk the walk, Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? Netochka, you... Are you making fun of Paimon!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since you're already feeling well enough to joke around... Hmph, and here Paimon was, just a bit, a tiiiny bit, worried about you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Quick, say thank you to Paimon.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: #Mm! Thank you, Paimon, and thank you too, {NICKNAME}. Snowy Owl, Goldfinch, you're both my dear companions!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, what are your plans after this? And, the Proof of the Cognoscenti...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I'll let you take the Proof this time. You've earned it. But if we cross paths elsewhere in the future, don't expect any mercy from me, alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? So we'll be rivals next time we meet? Hehe, the two of us are formidable rivals to have, y'know!

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: It's a shame we can't become best companions, but I'll work hard to become your greatest rival instead. Just you wait and see!

choices.text: Don't overthink it. Do what makes you happy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't get it. Rather than thinking about things like fate or destiny... isn't it better to live happily?

talks.objective: Look for clues in the archives

dialogues.speaker: Locked Door
dialogues.text: (It won't budge at all. Looks like there's no way to open it...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not sure if there's another way out. Let's keep looking.

talks.objective: Find a way to open the gate

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Goldfinch! Just a little longer!

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: ...There we go! Goldfinch, the hammer is yours! Smash that big guy into pieces!

talks.objective: Use the destruction module to defeat opponents
Use the destruction module to reach the upper floor
Go to the second floor of the disposal workshop

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Sorry, I made trouble for you again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're used to it at this point. Now, if you ditched us or tried to shoo us off at this point... Now that would make us mad!

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: ...Okay. Then, thank you, for keeping me company.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's more like it! Speaking of, didn't that Ras guy say he'd meet us at the highest point? Why's the lift malfunctioning, then?

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: What should we do? Do we try to fix it?

choices.text: Knocking on it a few times might do the trick.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I doubt it's that easy to fix!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That scared Paimon! She thought it'd hit her for sure...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Oh! I've heard about this strange lightning before. A treasure hunter I met told me that, with the Moonstriders, it should be easy to jump from where the lightning strikes to the top level.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I guess you can fly up, Snowy Owl, but what about you, Goldfinch...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have my ways.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah! This is child's play for {M#him}{F#her}, but you might have to wait a bit.

choices.text: The Moonstriders are our best shot.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Um... I don't think they'll manage that far up. If we had some other help, though...

talks.objective: Find a way to enter an empowered state
Move the cleaning bot to a suitable location

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everything should be fine now, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Then I'll be off! Don't fall too far behind!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't get it. Rather than thinking about things like fate or destiny... isn't it better to live happily?

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: There's nothing here — but how... Did you find anything on your end?

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: Sorry, I made trouble for you again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're used to it at this point. Now, if you ditched us or tried to shoo us off at this point... Now that would make us mad!

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: ...Okay. Then, thank you, for keeping me company.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's more like it! Speaking of, didn't that Ras guy say he'd meet us at the highest point? Why's the lift malfunctioning, then?

dialogues.speaker: Netochka
dialogues.text: What should we do? Do we try to fix it?

choices.text: Knocking on it a few times might do the trick.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: I doubt it's that easy to fix!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That scared Paimon! She thought it'd hit her for sure...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Now we can jump up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! True, we did something similar when we collected data for Fanngel. But, what about Netochka...?

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Hm? You knew about this strange lightning, too? A treasure hunter I met told me that jumping from where the lightning strikes to the top level should be a cinch with the Moonstriders.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Should we go now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I need to do some prep first...

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Then I'll wait for you.

choices.text: The Moonstriders are our best shot.

response.speaker: Netochka
response.text: Um... I don't think they'll manage that far up. If we had some other help, though...

dialogues.speaker: "Nod-Krai Regional Safety Assessment Report"
dialogues.text: (A few thick volumes...)

dialogues.speaker: "Staff Casualty, Reward, and Punishment Records"
dialogues.text: (The section about the Nothing Passage seems quite intriguing...)

dialogues.speaker: Chatty Fatuus
dialogues.text: Say, the good ol' Poruchik collecting the <color=#00E1FFFF>Proof of the Cognoscenti</color>... Think that counts as an abuse of power for personal gain? I mean, we're here on a mission. The heck are we doing, digging holes for him like moles...

dialogues.speaker: Taciturn Fatuus
dialogues.text: What happens up there is none of our business.

dialogues.speaker: Chatty Fatuus
dialogues.text: Do you think reporting it to the higher-ups will do anything?

dialogues.speaker: Chatty Fatuus
dialogues.text: 'Cause it seems to me that they don't like <color=#00E1FFFF>Poruchik Raskolnikov</color> up there either. Maybe my report's just the opportunity they'll need!

dialogues.speaker: Taciturn Fatuus
dialogues.text: You should keep these words to yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Chatty Fatuus
dialogues.text: Huh? What, are you trying to get ahead of me? That's low of you, real low!

dialogues.speaker: Taciturn Fatuus
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Never mind that now, let's find a place to hide before we get caught!
I don't know where the other card is... but even if you find it, there's still the problem of <color=#00E1FFFF>getting it inside and placing it high up</color> to remove the barrier.
It boggles my mind why the Fatui would invent such a strange device...
